Rental Rogues

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Rental rogues are stealing the identity of estate agents and ripping off cash strapped South Africans in search of reasonable accommodation

Unique Selling Point:
All the characters will tell their stories, private company doing what the police should be doing and handing over information and still the scammers continue to operate. Warning to viewers - CB fighting the good fight to protect cash strapped South Africans

Summary:
Summary
Gerhard Kotze is a frustrated man, as CEO of a national estate agency Real net he has been trying to protect his agents and his company’s reputation from rental scammers but to no avail as the banks and the police do nothing to stop these scammers. Two of his agents Mike Dobbin and Stephan Loubser, one in CT, the other in Johannesburg have had their photos and some of their online information stolen and used. And its them that get the angry calls from people who realise they have lost deposit money to scammers. But there is nothing the agents can do – they too are victims of crime as their information is used fraudulently to trick desperate accommodation seekers to part with cash. This weekend was awful says Dobbin who was contacted by three different people. Two had lost money, the third he saved the day. “ I have even thought of changing my name or getting out of the industry” he says. Mike opened a case at the Cleveland police station but the police closed it because they told him he hasn’t lost anything.
Stephan says he knows when the landline rings its someone who has been scammed. He is quite a character and answers the phone saying: “Yes you have been scammed, no its not me and I hope you didn’t hand over any money!”


Further information:
Further information:
The scammers target their victims on the website rent uncle. They say that there is quite a demand for the property and insist on an administration fee before they can view it. They go in cheaper than the going rate says Loubser- a 2 bedroom in Durbanville goes for about R12 000, not R8 000 as the scammers advertise. They use Loubser or Dobbin’s details and photographs and the Realnet name but they change the email address and the logo is slightly different. But many people don’t double check and phone the agent on the correct number on the real website. People are losing thousands this way. Andrea Gibbon and her sister pulled together a deposit and the admin fee and paid over R13 000 for what looked like the perfect property for her mother. The photo’s of the property were real but stolen from elsewhere, the property wasn’t for rent and Loubser was not the agent. But he soon got the call and he repeated the story. You have been scammed. People are told that if they dont like the property they will get a full refund and the money will go towards their rental. None of that is true, once you pay into the bank accounts they give you – they disappear

No one is doing anything
Gerhard Kotze then paid a PI to trace some of the numbers. Chris Breedt gathered a lot of information and he says all the police had to do was follow it up and they would have been able to crack the syndicate, but alas they have done nothing.

Gerhard also tried to make rent uncle accountable, but it’s a black online hole that hasn’t responded and continues to provide a platform for the scammers, even as we go into 2023.

THE BANK
Stephan says the banks should easily be able to trace the perpetrators and questions why as agents they are strictly governed by FICA and the banks should be too. How is it possible he says that the banks dont have genuine ID numbers and proof of addresses of the scammers, because they are constantly opening new bank accounts. NEDBANK, STANDARD BANK and TYME BANK have all been used.

Carte Blanche speaks to the property agents, the victims, the PI and asks the police and the banks why they are ignoring a syndicate praying on South Africans.

FINAL SCRIPT Rental Rogues TX Sunday 5th February 2023

Voice over one
Real Estate companies are on high alert, and if you are about to rent a property – you need to be too.

Because the agent you think you’re talking to, may have had his identity stolen

Mike
They have my WhatsApp photo’s, they have my profile photos from my for sale boards, my email signature that I use

Voice over Two
Across the country, estate agents, and accommodation seekers have become the new targets for scammers

Stefan
So I think my number plate should be scam WP, and I am really an honest person

Voice over Three
And even the cautious are being duped in their search for affordable accommodation

Derek
Are you embarrassed by this?
Lauren Gibbon
Oh most definitely. I have never been a victim of an online scams before and I always double check everything.

Fade to black

LINK
This scam has two parts to it. To lure their victims the scammers need legitimacy, and this is easily found – estate agents and rental agents have all their details and even their photographs online

Voice over Four
Those details are used to trick victims to hand over money on existing properties, that aren’t available for rent

For Realnet properties MD Gerhard Kotze, the first signs of trouble came 6 months ago

Up sound Gerhard
I am phoning in connection with that scam...

Voice over Five
People were starting to think their agents were thieves. Realnet suddenly had a brand problem

Gerhard Kotze
It is negative for us Derek, that is why we need to stop it, our agents are going to be victimized and labelled by consumers and they saying this Mike Dobbin from Real Net is a thief, and the emotional trauma that is causing for the agent, its devasting

Voice over six
Mike Dobbin sells houses in Johannesburg’s eastern suburbs, but his name was being used by criminals in the Cape

Mike Dobbin
I have thought of using one of my other names and changing my online profile. I have actually even thought about getting out of this industry.

Voice over seven
Durbanville, a 30 minute drive north of Cape Town is bursting at the seams. It’s good for Stefan Loubser a successful rental agent in the area

Derek
The market is flourishing?
Stefan
Yah, its booming, one listing gets like twenty to thirty enquiries. I will list it in the morning, my phone will go crazy, then I will remove the listing, pick and choose who I am going to let view, then usually about five couples view, and all five want the property

Voice over eight
But around September last year, his landline exploded with enraged South Africans who accused him of stealing their money

Up sound
Stefan Loubser speaking

Derek
So what was your first reaction when you get those calls
Stefan
When they say are you Stefan Loubser? I say you’ve been scammed! And 100% of the time the second sentence is yes we paid money

Voice over nine
In early January, sisters Lauren and Andrea Gibbon began searching for a small affordable rental for their mom, but they couldn’t find one.

Lauren
I started by looking online – complexes were pricey so I took to the net to see if there were any ads that were within our price range


Voice over ten
They found the perfect rental on this site, RENT UNCLE. They were familiar with the complex and at R4800 per month it was within budget.

Derek
So were you shown pictures?
Lauren
Yes we were, and as you can see these are the pictures one could view
Derek
Beautiful gardens
Lauren
And it was advertised through a legitimate real estate agency

Voice over eleven
The company named on the website advert was Real NET properties.

But before they could view the flat, they were asked to fill in documentation and go through a credit check process.

Andrea
Derek it was very thorough. They asked for 3 months bank statements, they asked for my employee details, banking details, payslips. So basically all my information, I provided it to them

Voice over twelve
Unknowingly Andrea had just sent all her documents to a criminal syndicate even though she signed forms with a REALNET logo on them. And she was by no means the first

Gerhard
At first we thought it wasn’t a big thing or maybe a once off, but then we realized there’s many people, maybe two, three, four cases a day coming in and those are the ones that actually report this

Voice over thirteen
By mid-January, the Gibbon sisters were excited, their application had been approved. They paid over the admin fee and a deposit of R8500 rand – hoping to sign the lease and view the property

Derek
Why did you hand over substantial amount of money before viewing this alleged apartment?
Lauren
In receiving the documentation to say we had been approved, made to believe other people were looking at the property, and if we hadn’t secured that confirmation deposit it would be handed to the next approved person


Derek
Did they offer you a refund if you didn’t like the place?
Lauren
Yes, so what they said was, once viewing the property if we still didn’t like what we saw, the money they had received would be reimbursed back to us.

Voice over 14
And to add plausibility to the scam, a big red approval stamp on the documents

Gerhard
Derek they are getting better, better at this every day. They actually created a beautiful you have been approved rental stamp which we don’t have, but I really like it I am going to use it
Derek
You going to pinch from the scammers?
He laughs
Derek
How low can you go Gerhard! It looks authoritative, if there is a stamp on it and it’s a red stamp, it must be.

LINK
Real net is not the only estate agency impacted, but Gerhard decided to take action. He hired a PI- who managed to find out who the scammers were personally linked to – then they handed all that information to the police – hoping for a breakthrough

Chris Breedt Up sound

Voice over fifteen
Chris Breedt has been gathering intelligence for 30 years, first in the military and now as a PI. Real Net gave him the bank account numbers and cell numbers

Chris
There is always a trace, always a means of getting information

Voice over sixteen
The scammers may have used untraceable numbers, but their close associates didn’t and the PI tracked down those individuals addresses

Chris
You don’t get scammed late at night early mornings, calling someone late at night and mornings then we gather it’s a girlfriend or a wife

Voice over seventeen
The investigation took him to a suburb in Bloemfontein and appeared to lead to prisoners or correctional service officials.

Sophisticated scams are being run from inside some of our prisons, as we revealed in a previous Carte Blanche investigation. So Chris hoped the police would be proactive.

Chris
Straightforward intelligence gathering, normal investigative work, all he had to do was execute it

Voice over eighteen
But nothing was followed up and six months later the scammers were successfully scamming the Gibbon sisters, promising them that an agent called Stefan Loubser would show them around – of course the real Stefan knew nothing about it

Stefan
Never ever look for a property on RentUncle.com and you never pay money before viewing unless you know it’s a reputable agency.

Voice over nineteen
The scammers had already been paid money but now they pushed for the first months rental too. Only then would the viewing take place

Lauren
I phoned my sister and said it doesn’t sound right, but it was four in the afternoon and I know I needed to get money in order to get confirmation that we had secured the place

Voice over twenty
And so they paid a total of R14 500 before realising they had been scammed.

Andrea
I was in absolute shock. There were definitely cues that we should have picked up on
Derek
So you were effectively conned twice?
Lauren
Yes, so we were conned with the payments, we were conned with the fact that it was an immediate thing you could rent, and on the day of signing at the viewing you could then get the keys to the property.

LINK
So another day, another online scam, but who is stopping these con artists?

Voice over 21
Not the police says Gerhard Kotze

Derek
Gerhard a number of clients have gone to the police have they had any joy?
Not to date no
Nothing
Derek
Nothing!

Voice over 22
And they didn’t help Mike Dobbin either

Mike
With regards to my case of stolen Identity, they informed me they are closing the case, I felt abandoned and a sense of desperation, what do I do?

Voice over 23
Both Stefan and Mike who live daily with the impact of stolen identities, believe banks could do more

Stefan Loubser
So my question is how can the banks not trace anything back to the people receiving scam money, because they have been opening bank accounts from numerous well known banks

Voice over 24
As the scammers run riot, Gerhard says you can protect yourself by asking an agent for their fidelity fund number
Gerhard
you can google that and it will take you into the regulatory authority website and you can see that it is a legitimate agent- don’t deal with them it’s probably a scam
Derek
How much do you think the scammers have made out of this?
Gerhard
A lot of money! Derek so, the average loss per client that we have dealt with is between R8000 and ranges anything up to R30 000. If you take the scam and multiply it across SA the way they doing it in Cape Town surrounding at the moment, it will be millions.

Voice over 25
Meanwhile Chris Breedt is hard at work – tracking and tracing the fake agent that duped the Gibbon sisters. He has names and addresses which have led him to Rustenburg. All he needs now is for the police to do their job

THE END 11: 00


PROMO ONE 11 seconds
Voice over
Conniving criminals are stealing the identities of legitimate estate agents and conning South Africans to pay upfront deposits on fake rentals







PROMO TWO 21 seconds

Voice over
Beware the affordable rental accommodation you find online

Derek
So were you shown pictures?
Lauren
Yes we were, and as you can see these are the pictures one could view, And it was advertised through a legitimate real estate agency

Voice over
Rental Scammers are impersonating reputable companies and duping South Africans


PROMO THREE 21 seconds

Voice over
A property company becomes the target of criminals that steal their agents identity

Derek
Gerhard a number of clients have gone to the police have they had any joy?
Gerhard
Not to date no

Voice over
Why haven’t the police followed up on vital information they are given by a private investigator

Chris
Straightforward intelligence gathering, normal investigative work, all he had to do was execute it

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Rental rogues are stealing the identity of estate agents and ripping off cash strapped South Africans in search of reasonable accommodation
metadata.Unique Selling Point: All the characters will tell their stories, private company doing what the police should be doing and handing over information and still the scammers continue to operate. Warning to viewers - CB fighting the good fight to protect cash strapped South Africans
metadata.Summary: Summary Gerhard Kotze is a frustrated man, as CEO of a national estate agency Real net he has been trying to protect his agents and his company’s reputation from rental scammers but to no avail as the banks and the police do nothing to stop these scammers. Two of his agents Mike Dobbin and Stephan Loubser, one in CT, the other in Johannesburg have had their photos and some of their online information stolen and used. And its them that get the angry calls from people who realise they have lost deposit money to scammers. But there is nothing the agents can do – they too are victims of crime as their information is used fraudulently to trick desperate accommodation seekers to part with cash. This weekend was awful says Dobbin who was contacted by three different people. Two had lost money, the third he saved the day. “ I have even thought of changing my name or getting out of the industry” he says. Mike opened a case at the Cleveland police station but the police closed it because they told him he hasn’t lost anything. Stephan says he knows when the landline rings its someone who has been scammed. He is quite a character and answers the phone saying: “Yes you have been scammed, no its not me and I hope you didn’t hand over any money!”
metadata.Further information: Further information: The scammers target their victims on the website rent uncle. They say that there is quite a demand for the property and insist on an administration fee before they can view it. They go in cheaper than the going rate says Loubser- a 2 bedroom in Durbanville goes for about R12 000, not R8 000 as the scammers advertise. They use Loubser or Dobbin’s details and photographs and the Realnet name but they change the email address and the logo is slightly different. But many people don’t double check and phone the agent on the correct number on the real website. People are losing thousands this way. Andrea Gibbon and her sister pulled together a deposit and the admin fee and paid over R13 000 for what looked like the perfect property for her mother. The photo’s of the property were real but stolen from elsewhere, the property wasn’t for rent and Loubser was not the agent. But he soon got the call and he repeated the story. You have been scammed. People are told that if they dont like the property they will get a full refund and the money will go towards their rental. None of that is true, once you pay into the bank accounts they give you – they disappear No one is doing anything Gerhard Kotze then paid a PI to trace some of the numbers. Chris Breedt gathered a lot of information and he says all the police had to do was follow it up and they would have been able to crack the syndicate, but alas they have done nothing. Gerhard also tried to make rent uncle accountable, but it’s a black online hole that hasn’t responded and continues to provide a platform for the scammers, even as we go into 2023. THE BANK Stephan says the banks should easily be able to trace the perpetrators and questions why as agents they are strictly governed by FICA and the banks should be too. How is it possible he says that the banks dont have genuine ID numbers and proof of addresses of the scammers, because they are constantly opening new bank accounts. NEDBANK, STANDARD BANK and TYME BANK have all been used. Carte Blanche speaks to the property agents, the victims, the PI and asks the police and the banks why they are ignoring a syndicate praying on South Africans.
